newsitem.title: CHINA: Competition prompts price cuts by China car makers.
newsitem.headline: Competition prompts price cuts by China car makers.

text.p: China's car makers have cut their prices because of fierce competition in a sluggish market, the Economic Information Daily said on Monday.
Guangzhou Peugeot Automobile, a venture by France's Peugeot S.A., had cut the price of its sedans by 3.1 percent since January and by 4.6 percent compared with June last year, the newspaper said.
The price of mini-sedans built by Tianjin Automobile Co had fallen 3.7 percent in June compared with the price early this year and was down 8.1 percent compared with the year-ago period, it said.
Shanghai Volkswagen, a joint venture involving German auto giant Volkswagen AG, had cut the price of its Santana 2000 sedan by 2.1 percent since early in the year, it said.
The newspaper gave no details of current prices.
Many Chinese vehicle makers have struggled to find profits in recent years as demand fails to keep up with growing capacity, prompting fierce price competition.
Beijing said early this month it would tighten its control over the sprawling automobile sector to try to ease excess capacity and increase efficiency.
